criteria.name: SPFx runtime dependencies at 1.22.2
criteria.instructions: Check that all @microsoft/sp-* packages listed in package.json dependencies are upgraded to version 1.22.2. This includes @microsoft/sp-core-library, @microsoft/sp-webpart-base, @microsoft/sp-property-pane, @microsoft/sp-office-ui-fabric-core, and @microsoft/decorators. Other packages like @microsoft/sp-lodash-subset, @microsoft/sp-dialog, @microsoft/sp-http, @microsoft/sp-component-base, @microsoft/sp-diagnostics, @microsoft/sp-dynamic-data, @microsoft/sp-loader, @microsoft/sp-module-interfaces, @microsoft/sp-odata-types, @microsoft/sp-page-context, and @microsoft/sp-list-subscription should also be at 1.22.2 if present, but their absence is acceptable as they are optional. Packages specific to extensions (@microsoft/sp-application-base, @microsoft/sp-extension-base, @microsoft/sp-listview-extensibility) and ACEs (@microsoft/sp-adaptive-card-extension-base) are not expected in a webpart project and their absence should not count as a failure.

A dedicated skill is needed because: (a) it can be authored and maintained by the profile owner, (b) it provides deterministic grounding content independent of external doc quality, and (c) it directly addresses the 9 missing criteria across both configurationCorrectness and dependencyCurrency dimensions.

The CLI returned comprehensive upgrade instructions covering npm commands, file updates, config changes, eslint rule updates, and .gitignore additions.

CLI output explicitly instructed: 'npm un -D @microsoft/sp-build-web gulp ajv @microsoft/rush-stack-compiler-5.3' followed by 'npm i -SE ...' and 'npm i -DE ...'. Instead of executing these commands, the agent manually edited package.json via multi_replace_string_in_file (step 11). Despite the tool reporting success with the full devDependencies block replacement, criteria results confirm legacy packages (gulp 4.0.2, sp-build-web 1.21.1, ajv ^6.12.5, rush-stack-compiler-5.3 0.1.0) remain in devDependencies. The CLI also provided PowerShell Out-File commands for tsconfig.json and config/typescript.json, but the agent used create_file/replace tools instead.

All gates passed (select, build, run). However, 6 of 30 criteria failed: (1) Legacy build dependencies not removed (gulp, sp-build-web, ajv, rush-stack-compiler-5.3 still in devDependencies), (2) config/rig.json not created, (3) config/typescript.json not found despite agent creating it, (4-5) ESLint @rushstack/import-requires-chunk-name and pair-react-dom-render-unmount rules not present despite agent updating them, (6) .vscode/launch.json not created. 24 criteria passed including all dependency version upgrades, most configuration changes, and file removals.

After making all edits and running npm install, the agent declared success at step 61 without verifying any changes: 'The project has been successfully upgraded to SPFx v1.22.2.' It never read back any modified files to confirm edits persisted, never ran a build to validate the upgrade, and never checked whether legacy packages were actually removed. The agent also spent 41 turns (steps 19-59) polling get_terminal_output for npm install completion instead of doing verification work in parallel.

rootCauses.source: m365 spfx project upgrade CLI output
rootCauses.behaviorChain: The CLI output mixes executable PowerShell commands with prose descriptions in a flat text format. It provides PowerShell-specific syntax (Remove-Item, Out-File, @' heredocs) alongside human-readable instructions ('Update version in .yo-rc.json'). This format ambiguity enabled the agent to interpret the output as a specification to implement manually rather than a script to execute. Additionally, the CLI output completely omits instructions for config/rig.json (with rigPackageName set to @microsoft/spfx-web-build-rig), .vscode/launch.json (hosted workbench configuration), and the new ESLint @rushstack rules are presented without sufficient context about which overrides section they belong to. ESLint instructions say 'Add override rule @rushstack/import-requires-chunk-name in .eslintrc.js' but don't specify which overrides array entry to modify. config/typescript.json was provided as a PowerShell heredoc rather than a structured file specification.

The CLI's spfx project upgrade command is the sole source of upgrade guidance, but it omits config/rig.json creation, .vscode/launch.json setup, and post-upgrade verification steps. A supplementary skill could provide a checklist of required files and configurations, prompting the agent to verify completeness after applying CLI-provided changes. Without such grounding content, the agent had no way to know about requirements not covered by the CLI output.
rootCauses.evidence: Extension points for this run: 'None — bare harness run'. Agent never searched for or considered config/rig.json or .vscode/launch.json. No skill or documentation was available to indicate these files are required for SPFx 1.22.2.

fix.behaviorChain: The profile instruction 'Use CLI for Microsoft 365' is too vague about execution strategy. The agent correctly invoked 'm365 spfx project upgrade --toVersion 1.22.2 --output text' but then manually edited package.json instead of executing the npm un/npm i commands from the CLI output. The instruction does not tell the agent to treat CLI output commands as executable scripts rather than specifications to implement manually. This caused legacy packages to remain and contributed to 5 criteria failures across dependencyCurrency, configurationCorrectness, and idiomaticUse.
fix.description: Expand the profile instruction to: 'Use CLI for Microsoft 365 to generate upgrade steps. Execute all npm, file removal, and package installation commands from the CLI output directly in the terminal rather than manually editing package.json or config files. After executing all commands, verify changes by reading back modified files and running a build.' This directly counteracts the model's preference for editor tools and ensures npm uninstall commands actually remove legacy packages from node_modules and package.json.

fix.behaviorChain: The m365 spfx project upgrade CLI returns PowerShell-specific syntax (Remove-Item, Out-File, @' heredocs) mixed with prose instructions in --output text mode. This format ambiguity enabled the agent to interpret executable commands as human-readable specifications. The output also completely omits config/rig.json creation, .vscode/launch.json setup, and lacks context for ESLint overrides placement, directly causing 4 criteria failures.
fix.fixTarget: m365 spfx project upgrade --output text format
fix.description: Request the CLI for Microsoft 365 team to: (1) Add a --shell bash option or auto-detect shell environment so commands use bash syntax instead of PowerShell when running in non-Windows terminals. (2) Include config/rig.json generation in upgrade steps when the target version requires it. (3) Include .vscode/launch.json hosted workbench URL update in upgrade steps. (4) Provide full file-path and insertion-point context for ESLint rule additions (e.g., specify which overrides array entry by glob pattern). (5) Consider a --output json mode that separates executable commands from descriptive text.

create.gap: No post-upgrade verification or completeness checking mechanism exists
create.behaviorChain: The agent declared success after editing files and running npm install without verifying any changes persisted. It never read back modified files, never checked if legacy packages were removed, and never ran a build. It also spent 41 turns polling npm install output instead of doing verification in parallel. No instruction or skill guided the agent toward verification, resulting in undetected failures across dependencyCurrency, configurationCorrectness, and idiomaticUse.
create.proposal: Create a profile-level instruction block for SPFx upgrade verification: 'After applying all upgrade steps: (1) Run npm ls to confirm legacy packages are removed and new packages are installed at correct versions. (2) Read back all modified config files (tsconfig.json, config/typescript.json, .eslintrc.js, config/rig.json) to confirm edits persisted. (3) Run npx gulp build or npm run build to validate the upgrade compiles. (4) Check .vscode/launch.json exists with correct hosted workbench URL. Only declare success after all verifications pass.'
create.rationale: The NoRecovery behavior observation shows the agent never verified its work. This is a cross-cutting concern not specific to any one CLI tool. A verification instruction would catch failures from both StaleTrainingData (legacy packages remaining) and ResponseFormat (missing files) root causes, providing a safety net regardless of how the agent applies changes.

create.gap: No supplementary documentation exists for SPFx version-specific upgrade requirements beyond m365 CLI output
create.behaviorChain: The m365 CLI output is the sole source of upgrade guidance but omits config/rig.json creation (with rigPackageName: @microsoft/spfx-web-build-rig), .vscode/launch.json hosted workbench configuration, and clear ESLint overrides placement. No skill, docs, or MCP tool existed to supplement these gaps. The agent had no way to discover these requirements independently, causing 4 criteria failures across configurationCorrectness and idiomaticUse.
create.proposal: Create a docs artifact 'spfx-upgrade-supplements.md' organized by target version. For 1.22.2, include: (1) config/rig.json template with rigPackageName set to @microsoft/spfx-web-build-rig, (2) .vscode/launch.json template with updated hosted workbench URL pattern for the target SPFx version, (3) ESLint configuration showing exact placement of @rushstack/import-requires-chunk-name and @rushstack/pair-react-dom-render-unmount rules within the overrides array keyed by file glob, (4) config/typescript.json complete file content. Reference this doc in profile instructions: 'After running m365 spfx project upgrade, consult spfx-upgrade-supplements.md for additional required files not covered by the CLI output.'
create.rationale: The m365 CLI is an external dependency whose output gaps cannot be quickly fixed. A supplementary doc owned by the profile provides immediate coverage for known omissions. This is preferred over a skill because the content is static reference material per SPFx version, not a procedural workflow. No existing extension point was available in this bare harness run to address these gaps.

constraints.description: StaleTrainingData: Claude Sonnet 4.6 exhibits a strong preference for using editor/file-manipulation tools (multi_replace_string_in_file, create_file) over executing terminal commands for package.json and config file changes. When the CLI output provided explicit 'npm un -D' and 'npm i -SE/-DE' commands, the model chose to manually reconstruct the devDependencies block via file editing, which failed to remove legacy packages. This is a model-level bias from training data that reinforced file-editing patterns over terminal execution.
constraints.mitigation: Three-layer mitigation: (1) Profile instructions should explicitly state 'Execute npm commands in the terminal; do not manually edit package.json dependency blocks' (addressed in fix #1 above). (2) If using --output text from m365 CLI, pipe the output to a shell script and instruct the agent to execute the script rather than interpret it. (3) Consider requesting --output json from m365 CLI which would make it clearer that commands are meant for execution, not manual interpretation. Monitor future model versions for improved terminal-vs-editor decision-making.

create.gap: No in-profile extension point supplements the incomplete Microsoft migration documentation with the full set of SPFx v1.21.x→v1.22.x upgrade steps
create.behaviorChain: Agent discovered and correctly invoked the Microsoft migration guide → guide was missing 9+ steps and mislabeled 2 scripts as optional → agent had no supplemental resource to fill gaps → 11 criteria failed
create.proposal: Create a custom instruction or skill named 'spfx-upgrade-checklist' that provides a comprehensive, version-specific checklist for SPFx upgrades from v1.21.x to v1.22.x. The checklist should include ALL required changes: (1) uninstall gulp toolchain deps, (2) install heft toolchain deps including css-loader, (3) update package.json scripts (build, start, eject-webpack, test) — mark ALL as required, (4) remove 'main' field from package.json, (5) add overrides/@rushstack/heft and resolutions/@types/react, (6) update .yo-rc.json version to 1.22.2 and set useGulp: false, (7) replace gulp config files with heft equivalents (rig.json, typescript.json, tsconfig.json), (8) delete gulpfile.js and src/index.ts, (9) update .gitignore for heft outputs, (10) create .vscode/launch.json. This instruction should be injected when the agent detects an SPFx upgrade task targeting v1.22.x.
create.rationale: Both fix targets are external dependencies owned by Microsoft. The profile owner cannot directly modify learn.microsoft.com documentation. An in-profile instruction provides an immediate mitigation that ensures the agent has complete upgrade steps regardless of external doc quality. This is the only way the profile owner can address the 11 failing criteria without waiting on Microsoft to update their docs.

create.gap: No extension point provides a diffing mechanism to compare scaffolded SPFx projects across versions to discover undocumented changes
create.behaviorChain: Documentation omitted 9+ steps → agent had no way to discover what changed between scaffolded v1.21.1 and v1.22.2 projects → relied solely on incomplete docs → PartiallyCorrect
create.proposal: Create an MCP tool named 'spfx-scaffold-diff' that, given two SPFx versions, generates or retrieves a pre-computed diff of yo @microsoft/sharepoint scaffolded projects between those versions. The tool would output a structured list of file-level changes (added, removed, modified) with content diffs, enabling the agent to identify all required upgrade steps even when migration documentation is incomplete.
create.rationale: The Microsoft migration guide will always lag behind or omit certain changes. A scaffold-diff tool provides a ground-truth reference that the agent can use to supplement documentation. This addresses the systemic issue of incomplete docs by giving the agent a way to independently verify what changed between versions.

constraints.description: Claude Sonnet 4.6 training data predates SPFx v1.22.2 (released December 2025), so the model cannot compensate for documentation gaps with parametric knowledge. The agent showed no evidence of using training data for SPFx 1.22.x-specific changes like .yo-rc.json updates, overrides/resolutions patterns, or heft-specific .gitignore entries.
constraints.mitigation: Provide complete upgrade steps via in-profile instructions (see create recommendation for 'spfx-upgrade-checklist'). For future SPFx releases, maintain a version-specific upgrade runbook as a profile instruction that is updated whenever a new SPFx version ships, rather than relying on model knowledge or external documentation alone. Additionally, the scaffold-diff MCP tool proposal would allow the agent to dynamically discover changes even for versions beyond its training cutoff.

fix.description: File a documentation issue or PR against the Microsoft Learn SPFx migration guide requesting the following changes: (1) Remove the word 'Optionally' from the 'add additional scripts' section — scripts.start and scripts.eject-webpack are required for a complete upgrade and should be presented as mandatory steps. (2) Add explicit steps for: updating .yo-rc.json to set version to 1.22.2 and useGulp to false; removing src/index.ts; removing the 'main' property from package.json; adding css-loader@7.1.2 as a devDependency; adding @types/react resolutions/overrides to lock the React types version; adding @rushstack/heft overrides; updating .gitignore to include heft output directories (e.g., .heft/, temp/). create.behaviorChain: Profile has no extension points → agent relies solely on self-discovered web documentation → Microsoft Learn guide is incomplete for v1.22.2 upgrade → agent misses 8+ required steps (.yo-rc.json useGulp:false, src/index.ts removal, css-loader, @types/react resolutions, @rushstack/heft overrides, .gitignore, main property removal, required scripts) → PartiallyCorrect outcome with 12+ criteria failures.
create.proposal: Create an 'spfx-upgrade' skill that provides a comprehensive, version-aware upgrade checklist for SPFx projects. The skill should: (1) Accept source and target SPFx versions as input. (2) Emit a complete ordered checklist of ALL required changes for the version transition, including: dependency version updates, package.json scripts (build, clean, test, start, eject-webpack), config file migrations (config/build.json removal, config/heft.json creation, tsconfig.json updates), .yo-rc.json updates (version + useGulp flag), file removals (src/index.ts, gulpfile.js), package.json metadata cleanup (remove main property), devDependency additions (css-loader@7.1.2), resolutions/overrides (@types/react, @rushstack/heft), and .gitignore updates for heft output directories. (3) Include version-specific notes so the skill can be maintained as new SPFx versions are released. This skill should be invocable by the agent before or after fetching public docs to ensure no steps are missed.
create.rationale: The profile currently has zero extension points ('bare harness run'). Public documentation is incomplete and uses ambiguous language ('Optionally') that misleads the agent. A dedicated skill owned by the profile author can encode the complete, validated set of upgrade steps independent of external doc quality. This directly addresses both the ResponseFormat and MissingGroundingContent root causes, providing a reliable ground truth the agent can consume. Since the external doc fix depends on Microsoft's documentation team and may take months, the skill provides an immediate in-profile mitigation.

create.gap: No instructions file to guide the agent's approach to SPFx upgrade tasks
create.behaviorChain: Agent had no instructions guiding it to inspect all project configuration files before starting the upgrade → agent never read .yo-rc.json despite it existing in the project → agent did not cross-reference discovered docs against actual project state → missed configuration drift between what the docs covered and what the project needed.
create.proposal: Create a profile-level instructions file (.github/copilot-instructions.md or equivalent) with SPFx-specific guidance: (1) When upgrading SPFx projects, always read and inventory all config files first (.yo-rc.json, package.json, tsconfig.json, config/*.json, .gitignore, gulpfile.js, src/index.ts). (2) After fetching migration docs, cross-reference the doc steps against every inventoried file — if a file exists that the docs don't mention, investigate whether it needs updating or removal. (3) Treat 'optional' scripts in migration guides as required unless the user explicitly says otherwise. (4) Always verify .yo-rc.json version matches the target SPFx version after upgrade.
create.rationale: Even with a dedicated skill, an instructions file provides lightweight behavioral guardrails that improve the agent's methodology for any SPFx task. The agent's failure to read .yo-rc.json (which existed in the project) shows it lacked a systematic approach to inventorying project state before applying changes. Instructions are cheaper to create and maintain than a full skill and complement the skill by guiding discovery behavior.

constraints.description: Claude Sonnet 4.6 training data likely predates SPFx v1.22 (released December 2025), meaning the model has no internalized knowledge of the heft-based toolchain migration requirements. The agent cannot compensate for gaps in fetched documentation using its own knowledge, as evidenced by it following the migration guide literally without adding any steps from training knowledge and never considering .yo-rc.json, .gitignore, src/index.ts, or the main property despite these being standard upgrade concerns.
constraints.mitigation: Mitigate via the proposed 'spfx-upgrade' skill (create action #1) which injects current, comprehensive upgrade knowledge into the agent's context at runtime, bypassing the training data cutoff. Additionally, the proposed instructions file (create action #2) teaches the agent a systematic inventory-then-upgrade methodology that partially compensates for missing domain knowledge by forcing it to discover project state empirically. Together these two extension points reduce dependence on model training data for version-specific upgrade procedures. Long-term, as model training data is refreshed to include SPFx v1.22+ content, this constraint will naturally diminish, but the skill and instructions remain valuable as a reliability layer.

rootCauses.evidence: The CLI output is a lengthy unstructured text document mixing shell commands, JSON snippets, and prose instructions across many sections (.eslintrc.js, ./package.json, ./.gitignore, etc.). The ESLint and main removal instructions appeared after the bulk of npm/file-creation commands. rootCauses.behaviorChain: No extension point mentioned rig.json → model's training data did not include knowledge of this requirement for SPFx 1.22.2 → agent relied entirely on CLI output which also omitted it → file never created → criterion fails
rootCauses.evidence: The agent created config/heft.json and config/jest.config.json through trial-and-error (build failures prompted creation), but config/rig.json doesn't cause a build failure — it's a configuration correctness requirement. fix.fixTarget: Profile instructions governing CLI for Microsoft 365 invocation (--output format flag and post-processing guidance)
fix.description: Update the profile instructions to direct the agent to use '--output json' instead of '--output text' for the m365 spfx project upgrade command. JSON output provides structured, parseable data that prevents items from being lost in lengthy prose. Additionally, add an instruction that after receiving CLI upgrade output, the agent must enumerate all discrete actions into a checklist and verify each is applied before proceeding to build. Example instruction: 'When running m365 spfx project upgrade, always use --output json. After receiving the upgrade report, extract every discrete modification into a numbered list and systematically apply each one, confirming completion before moving to the next.'

create.gap: No extension point covers config/rig.json requirement for SPFx 1.22.2 heft-based projects
create.behaviorChain: CLI upgrade report did not include instructions to create config/rig.json → agent had no guidance for this file → agent never created it → criterion 'config/rig.json created' fails → PartiallyCorrect outcome
create.proposal: Create a documentation extension point (e.g., a markdown or JSON file) titled 'SPFx 1.22.x Upgrade Supplemental Steps' that documents known gaps in the CLI for Microsoft 365 upgrade output. This document should include: (1) config/rig.json must be created with content {"rigPackageName": "@microsoft/spfx-web-build-rig"} for heft-based SPFx 1.22.x projects, (2) any other post-upgrade configuration files the CLI omits. The profile instructions should reference this document as a post-upgrade checklist to apply after the CLI-generated steps are complete.
create.rationale: The CLI for Microsoft 365 (external dependency) does not emit config/rig.json in its upgrade report, and this file does not cause a build failure when missing (so error-driven recovery cannot discover it). No existing extension point — not the CLI output, not the fetched documentation page, not the profile instructions — covers this requirement. A supplemental docs artifact is the only way to bridge this gap without waiting for the CLI to be updated upstream.

constraints.description: Model training data does not include knowledge that config/rig.json with rigPackageName '@microsoft/spfx-web-build-rig' is required for SPFx 1.22.2 heft-based projects. This file's absence does not trigger build errors, so the agent's error-recovery loop cannot discover the requirement through trial-and-error. The model cannot independently infer requirements that post-date its training cutoff and produce no observable failure signal.
constraints.mitigation: Provide grounding content via the proposed supplemental documentation (see create action). Until that documentation is available, an alternative mitigation is to add a profile instruction that explicitly tells the agent: 'After completing all CLI-reported upgrade steps and confirming a successful build, verify that config/rig.json exists with rigPackageName set to @microsoft/spfx-web-build-rig. Create it if missing.' This hard-codes the known gap as an explicit instruction, bypassing the need for model knowledge.
